leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - 2010 ruling on pride parade bans
leads.documents: Documents systemic discrimination by Russian cities refusing permits for pride parades; Court ruled decisions effectively approved groups calling for disruption.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'In 2010, the European Court of Human Rights fined Russia for discriminating against the LGBTQ community, after local governments systemically refused to issue permits to pride parades' and Alexeyev / Moscow Pride case

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council expert panel - report 13 April 2017
leads.documents: Documents wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya - regional enforcement precedent for North Caucasus including Dagestan.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'In a report issued on 13 April 2017, a panel of five expert advisors to the United Nations Human Rights Council condemned the wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya'

leads.title: Russian federal law on 'propaganda' of non-traditional sexual relationships (2013, expanded 2022)
leads.documents: Documents legal status criminalizing distribution of materials promoting non-traditional relationships and materials making minors interested in gender transition; expanded in 2022 to anyone regardless of age.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 2013 law criminalising distribution of 'propaganda' among minors; 'in 2022, the propaganda law was expanded to apply to anyone regardless of age group, and to also prohibit distribution of materials that make minors interested in gender transitions'

leads.title: Russian federal law July 2023 banning gender transition
leads.documents: Documents ban on gender-affirming care/surgery and legal gender recognition - core trans legal status.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'In July 2023, Russia enacted a law banning gender transition which prohibited both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright' and 'Transgender people are not allowed to change their legal gender, and gender-affirming care is banned'

leads.title: Supreme Court of Russia - November 2023 ruling designating 'international LGBT public movement' as extremist
leads.documents: Documents criminalization of LGBT activism/participation/symbols; leading/participating/financing/displaying symbols punishable by prison; added to unified list 22 March 2024.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'In November 2023, the Supreme Court issued a ruling designating the international LGBT public movement as an extremist group' and 'On 22 March 2024, the international LGBT social movement and its structural units was formally added to the unified list of terrorist and extremist organizations and persons'

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - Fedotova and Others v. Russia (2021)
leads.documents: Documents lack of any legal recognition for same-sex relationships as human rights violation; Russia left court in 2022.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'In the 2021 case Fedotova and Others v. Russia, the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg ruled that it was a violation of human rights for Russia not to offer any form of legal recognition to same-sex relationships. However, Russia left the court in 2022'

leads.title: Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) - report December 2018
leads.documents: Documents confirmation that persecution of LGBTQ persons in Chechnya took place and was ignored by authorities.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'A report released in December 2018 by the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) confirmed claims that persecution of LGBTQ persons had taken place and was ignored by authorities'

leads.title: Russian Constitution amendment - July 2020 banning same-sex marriage
leads.documents: Documents constitutional ban on same-sex marriage applicable federally including Dagestan.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'In July 2020, Russian voters approved a Constitution amendment banning same-sex marriage' and marriage defined as between man and woman

leads.title: ILGA-Europe Rainbow Index - 2016, 2019, 2024 rankings
leads.documents: Documents institutional assessment of LGBTQ rights machinery: Russia 2nd least friendly 2016, 46th of 49 in May 2019, worst of 49 in 2024.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'In 2016, Russia was rated the second least LGBTQ-friendly nation in Europe by ILGA-Europe' and 'In 2024, the status of LGBTQ rights in Russia was ranked the worst out of the 49 countries surveyed' and 'In May 2019, ILGA-Europe placed Russia in 46th place among 49'

leads.title: Reuters - March 2021 report on EU sanctions
leads.documents: Documents international enforcement response: EU imposed economic sanctions on two Chechen officials accused of persecuting LGBTQ people.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'In March 2021, Reuters reported that the European Union imposed economic sanctions on two Chechen officials accused of persecuting LGBTQ people in Chechnya'
